E_c11_ss11_crosscheck.matrix_row: | **Curtain Wall** | ✅ `curtainwall.create` + `curtain-wall.batch.create` | ✅ §P3.1 (+ explicit `storeEventBus.emit`) | ⚠️ `CurtainWallStore.add()` omits storeEventBus — compensated by bridge emit | ✅ `'curtainwall'` | ✅ (Rev 4 — FIX-PLAN-VDT-BIMMANAGER-ALL-BRIDGES) | ✅ | ✅ FULL (TODO-CW-STORE-BUS active) |  (C11 §11, dated 2026-05-19)
E_c11_ss11_crosscheck.verdict: REFUTED on cell 3, cell 5's legend, and cell 1's spelling. The §11.1 gap row TODO-CW-STORE-BUS is ALSO refuted.
E_c11_ss11_crosscheck.refutation_cell_3: The matrix says `CurtainWallStore.add()` OMITS storeEventBus and is 'compensated by bridge emit'. MEASURED: `add()` (CurtainWallStore.ts:326-356) ends in `this.emit('add', …)` at :355, and `emit()` at :540-552 calls `storeEventBus.emit({elementType:'curtainwall', operation:'create'})` at :546. The store DOES emit. The bridge emit at initTools.ts:2129-2135 therefore is NOT a compensation — it is a DUPLICATE, and every mirrored curtain wall fires TWO plan-invalidation events. The code already says this (L-1056, initTools.ts:2118-2128) and further records that C87 §11 row 14 and CW-C-2 are derived from the same false premise and are refuted by it. The duplicate is retained deliberately, so the DEFECT IS THE DOC, not the code.
E_c11_ss11_crosscheck.refutation_ss11_1: §11.1 orders 'TODO-CW-STORE-BUS | Curtain Wall | Fix CurtainWallStore.add() to emit storeEventBus directly (eliminate bridge workaround) | Wave A16'. Half of that work is already done (the store emits) and doing the other half — deleting the bridge emit — is precisely the change L-1056 declined to make blind, because it reorders subscribers relative to the synchronous CurtainPanelSyncHandler storm inside add(). The row as written would authorise a rival, unwatched behaviour change.
E_c11_ss11_crosscheck.refutation_cell_1_spelling: The matrix names the CEB case `curtainwall.create`. MEASURED: the case is `case 'curtain-wall.create'` (CommandEventBridge.ts:694), hyphenated; `curtainwall.create` exists only as a handler ALIAS (CreateCurtainWall.ts:51). This is HARMLESS in effect — CommandBus stamps `type: handler.type` (the canonical name) on the record (CommandBus.ts:533), and probe P-10 confirms the alias still produces `curtain-wall.created` — but it is a false citation in a normative table, and it points a reader at a case that does not exist.
E_c11_ss11_crosscheck.refutation_cell_5_legend: The VDT+bimManager column legend says 'AFTER LegacyStore.add() (Bridge Invariant 7)'. Curtain wall registers BEFORE add (initTools.ts:2092/2094), by name and on purpose (§G3-STALE-FIX-CW, OI-054(a)). Following the legend literally would reintroduce the §G3-STALE storm it removed.
E_c11_ss11_crosscheck.what_the_matrix_gets_RIGHT: cells 2 (§P3.1 bridge exists), 4 ('curtainwall' in GEOMETRY_ELEMENT_TYPES) and the existence of the batch case.

F_findings.claim: C11 §11 cell 3 says `CurtainWallStore.add()` omits storeEventBus; it emits at :546 via :355. The 'compensation' at initTools:2129 is a documented duplicate (L-1056), so the matrix inverts the fact and §11.1 orders work whose first half is done and whose second half L-1056 declined.
`curtain-wall.create` with no `id` emits `curtain-wall.created id=undefined`; curtainWallCreatedMirror.ts:123 returns null. The plan tool's comment names the hazard, but nothing enforces it.
ZERO curtain-wall rows in ELEMENT_UPDATE_VERBS and 16 UNMIRRORED verbs in mirror-debt.json — more than any other family. Measured: `curtain-wall.resize` returns OK and emits no `element.updated`.

`curtain-wall.replacePanel` reads `ctx.stores['curtainPanelStore']`, a key no descriptor contributes, and declares `affectedStores: []` so the bus never throws — it refuses on every dispatch while two property panels and the AI classifier still offer it.
